Subject: Post-demo: pocket map request & quick econ-buyer + security ask

Hi Ethan — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and two asks so we can move this forward fast: 

Recap (very high level)
- Use case: generative summaries for claims intake + faster triage for clinical ops.
- Success criteria: sub-300ms p95 for triage flows, deterministic redaction of PHI, < $0.0008 per call target for pilot run.

Two asks from your side
1) Pocket map: could you share a short org/roster (PDF or simple chart) that lists who owns financial approval, security evidence, procurement, and the pilot sponsor (names + emails)? even a one-page diagram is perfect.
2) Fast security intro: who on your InfoSec side will do the initial vendor review? we typically send a 1–2 page security FAQ first — would save you time compared to a full questionnaire.

Also — if there are any hard constraints (data residency, required encryption at rest, mandatory audit windows) please flag them in the same file.

Proposed next steps
- If you can share the org chart + security contact, we’ll prepare a short technical brief and a one-page security FAQ for Perry to review.
- Tentative 30-min sync next week to introduce the econ buyer + security owner and walk the MAP.

Attachment: redwood_demo_notes_0816.pdf (1 page, short call notes)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching a couple of things that should help: AVAMED_orgchart_Q3.pdf (simple org chart) and procurement_playbook_v2.docx (internal procurement steps).

Quick answers inline:
- Econ buyer / final approver: Maria Santos (CFO) — maria.santos@avamed.com — she will own final purchase approval for pilots over $25k.
- Security reviewer: Perry Gomez (Director, InfoSec) — perry.gomez@avamed.com — he will kickoff the vendor security checklist and wants a short FAQ first.
- Procurement lead: Amira Kahn (Sourcing Manager) — amira.kahn@avamed.com — owns PO and vendor terms.
- Decision criteria: total cost of ownership (per inference economics), data handling & residency, SLA for uptime/latency, and reference checks from clinical customers.
- Timeline: internal review + econ buyer sync ~2 weeks; security review typically 3–4 weeks depending on workload; procurement/contract ~2–3 weeks after security signoff.

I can introduce Maria and Perry on this thread if that helps — would you like me to do that now or after you send the short security FAQ?

Attachments: AVAMED_orgchart_Q3.pdf (1 page), procurement_playbook_v2.docx (6 pages)

Best,
Ethan Young
Director, Clinical Ops | AvaMed Health

> I can introduce Maria and Perry on this thread if that helps — would you like me to do that now or after you send the short security FAQ?

Nice — thanks for the follow-up, Ethan.

Marissa / Sean — summary + recommended play:
- We should send Perry the security FAQ + the Redwood security one-pager (I attached an internal copy) to compress the security review timeline.
- Draft a short "pilot MAP" (mutual action plan) that lists milestones (technical kickoff, security review, pilot acceptance criteria, PO / legal). I can draft the financial asks based on the target per-call economics Marissa captured.
- If Maria (CFO) is the econ buyer, let's include a very short business case slide (1–2 bullets + expected $/month at pilot volumes) in the MAP.

Action items
1) Marissa: share the short security FAQ + proposed 30-min intro window for Maria / Perry.
2) Ben: I'll draft the MAP and a one-pager business case and hand to Lauren to own contract routing once we have procurement timeline.
3) Sean: prepare a brief technical 1-pager for Perry that highlights our encryption, KV caching, and prefix redaction controls.
